CausalChain: Nanoparticle conjugate (boron agent + immune adjuvant) -> selective tumor accumulation -> BNCT irradiation produces high LET radiation -> confined tumor cell damage leading to immunogenic cell death -> release of DAMPs and tumor antigens -> activation of dendritic cells -> T-cell priming -> enhanced local and systemic antitumor immune response (abscopal effect)
Hypothesis: A nanoparticle-based conjugate that co-delivers boron for BNCT and an immune-stimulatory adjuvant can synergistically enhance immunogenic cell death and activate systemic antitumor immunity, thereby improving outcomes in both primary and metastatic tumors.
Abstract: Recent advances in boron neutron capture therapy (BNCT) suggest that its tumor‐selective high linear energy transfer (LET) radiation may not only cause direct tumor cell damage but also trigger immunogenic cell death. We propose a novel paradigm in which a nanoparticle‐based conjugate co‐delivering a boron agent and an immune adjuvant is used to potentiate BNCT. This dual‐function agent is designed to concentrate within tumor tissue, where BNCT irradiation induces confined high LET damage that leads to the release of damage‐associated molecular patterns (DAMPs) and tumor antigens. Concurrent stimulation of the local immune microenvironment by the adjuvant component is hypothesized to amplify dendritic cell activation and T‐cell priming, thereby producing an enhanced local and systemic (abscopal) antitumor immune response. This combinatorial strategy may thereby improve control of both primary tumors and distant metastases.
